newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary stocks at fifth successive closing high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary stocks at fifth successive closing high.

text.p: Hungarian stocks rallied to their fifth successive closing high in busy trading on Tuesday, driven by the gains of heavy-weight stocks such as chemicals TVK, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 7,713.72 points according to preliminary figures, up 82,30 points or 1.08 percent, with 1,455,886 units traded on Tuesday.
Both domestic and foreign investoras were heavy buyers, traders said.

Recent heavy gains in Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) issues and BUX futures are encouraging domestic investors, while foreigners also heavily bought the stocks of large companies despite the dollar's overnight losses.

"Practically, it is difficult for foreign investors to find investment targets in the region outside Hungary...and Russia," said Gabor Sitanyi of London-based ING Barings, referring to trade account difficulties and floods in Poland and the Czech Republic and political uncertainties in Slovakia.
He added that Russia also attracted heavy foreign interest but investors limited the funds allocated to Russia due to the what they see as inherent risks in that market.

If the first half earnings reports to be published by August 15 justify expectations of good results, the bourse was likely to continue the six-month rally which has been interrupted by only small corrections, traders said.
"For example TVK seems to be very undervalued and (oil and gas company) MOL also expects good results," said Bence Peter of London Broker.
TVK traded in heavy turnover, with 576,059 units being sold, and extended Monday's gains to emd at 4,115 forints, up 115.
MOL shrugged off news that its bid for a 12.5 percent stakes in Croatia's Adriatic pipeline had failed and after an initial fall firmed to 4,395 forints, up 15 by the close.
Most other BSE issues followed these large companies, with 22 of them closing higher, nine falling and six remaining unchanged.

Traders said the market still did not seem overheated as Hungary's economic fundamentals and corporate results were improving, the dollar was strong and a general bullish trend prevailed on the world's stock markets.
"While Wall Street does not talk about overheating, neither will the Hungarian market," Sitanyi said.
